transcript.text: Hello, I'm Commander Gary Cuso of the Santa Ana Police Department.
What you are about to view is a critical incident community video briefing.
In the event of a critical incident, we strive to disseminate as much information as possible at the earliest opportunity contingent upon the progress of the investigation.
These briefings intend to provide the public with open and transparent communication regarding officer-involved critical incidents.
These briefings are based on the facts we know at the time of the video briefing.
They contain information obtained from numerous sources including, but not limited to, dispatch audio, video evidence, and witness or victim statements.

The Santa Ana Police Department takes any use of force by its officers very seriously and conducts thorough investigations into these incidents, often in conjunction with other investigative agencies.
These investigations typically require interviews with numerous witnesses, the review of video and audio evidence, and analyzing extensive amounts of forensic evidence.
As a result, these investigations can take up to a year to complete.
At this point in the investigation, no conclusion has been drawn whether our officers acted consistently with our policies and the law.
Please be advised, critical incidents are often high stress and emotional for those involved.
As a result of the stress and emotion, audio and video recordings may contain strong language,
and digital images may be graphic.
Warning, some viewers may find these videos disturbing and unsuitable for children.

Good evening I am Officer Natalie Garcia the Public Information Officer for the SAM Police Department I wish to provide you with a brief overview of an officer shooting that occurred on January 1st 2026 At 5 35 p
San Ana Police gang detectives were patrolling the area of 1600 South Evergreen Street due to
ongoing gang-related criminal activities affecting the community. As detectives entered the parking
lot adjacent to the east alley of 1600 South Evergreen Street, they observed a male in the
parking lot. The male noticed the marked Santa police vehicle and immediately turned the opposite
direction and began to flee. One of the detectives exited the passenger side of the police vehicle
and was involved in a foot pursuit. His partner continued driving the police vehicle. During the
foot pursuit, the detective identified himself as a police officer and ordered the male to stop.
The male disobeyed the detective's commands. The detective then observed the male holding a gun in
his right hand and repeatedly gave commands to drop the gun. However, the male disobeyed
the officer's commands and remained armed. The male suddenly turned in between two parked
vehicles, lowered his body to the ground, and presented the gun at the detective. To
de-escalate the situation, the detective made several verbal commands to the male to drop
the gun. Thereafter, an officer-involved shooting occurred. It was determined that the male was
not struck by gunfire. You will see segments of the body-worn camera footage. The identity and
personal identifying information of the reporting party has been redacted for privacy. Officers from
the San Antonio Police Department are issued body-worn cameras to be worn at chest level to
provide a general perspective of the officer. When the body-worn camera is activated, it goes back 30
seconds and starts recording. During this pre-record buffer, audio is not captured. This feature is
is designed to capture police activity that occurs suddenly.
It is important to understand that an officer's actions
can sometimes obscure the body-worn camera.

Sanana Police Dispatch was advised of the officer-involved shooting and additional officers responded to assist.
Orange County Fire Authority were also dispatched to the scene to administer medical aid to the suspect.
The suspect was taken to an area hospital for medical care.
You will now view images of the firearm recovered at the scene.
The weapon was a .38 Smith & Wesson revolver.
The suspect has been identified as a 17-year-old male who was subsequently booked at Juvenile Hall.
The Santa Ana Police Department is committed to transparency and aims to keep the public informed about critical incidents.
Over the impending months, three concurrent independent investigations will be undertaken.
The Orange County District Attorney's Office, responsible for investigating officer-involved shootings,
will continue its investigation into any potential criminal conduct by the officers involved.
Simultaneously, the Santa Ana Police Department's Internal Affairs Division will conduct an administrative investigation to assess whether the officers adhere to department policies and procedures
Additionally, the Santa Ana Police Department's Crimes Against Persons Division will investigate any alleged criminal conduct by the suspect
These investigative units will interview any witnesses and conduct any necessary forensic testing.
Upon the completion of the District Attorney's investigation, their office will issue a determination as to whether charges should be filed against the involved officers.
Thank you for taking the time to view this Critical Incident Community Briefing.
